Payday was Friday. It's Monday. Where did it go?

It's rarely one big purchase. It's a lot of small ones nobody wrote down. One way to stop the scramble is to give every dollar a job before the month starts. It takes about 20 minutes: income on top, bills under it, and whatever's left gets a name.

hook: The car repair never texts first.
caption:
The car repair never texts first.

In 2024, 63% of US adults said they'd cover a surprise $400 expense with cash or the equivalent (Federal Reserve). That means plenty of households would borrow or skip it. Surprise bills aren't really surprises, since cars break, kids outgrow shoes, and vets exist.

One way to handle it is a small line in the budget called "stuff that will happen." Start with whatever is honest this month. Even a small number counts. Save this for when the next thing breaks, and start your cushion with the free Your First $1,000 kit, linked in our bio.

(Source: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2024.)

hook: Money talks go better with snacks and a timer.
caption:
Money talks go better with snacks and a timer.

Most couples don't avoid money because they don't care. It just never feels like the right time. So pick the time, the same day each week, for fifteen minutes with phones face down. Minutes 1 to 5: what came in and what went out. Minutes 6 to 10: what's coming this week. Minutes 11 to 15: one thing to change. Just one.

Nobody gets blamed. You're both looking at the numbers, not at each other. Send this to your partner, and grab the free Your First $1,000 kit from the link in our bio to bring to your first money date.

Thanksgiving week is the first domino.

Groceries, travel, gifts, and a party or two all land in about five weeks, and none of it is a surprise. The trouble is that it gets spread across so many cards and receipts that nobody sees the total. One way to stay calm is to put a number on the whole season before you spend any of it: food, travel, gifts, events, then a total you can pay without borrowing.

hook: Black Friday has a deadline. Your budget doesn't.
caption:
Black Friday has a deadline. Your budget doesn't.

A sale feels like saving, but it only is if you were already going to buy it. Try the 24-hour rule: put it in the cart, close the app, and decide tomorrow. Keep a short wish list with a name next to each item. No name, no purchase. If it's on your list and inside your gift budget, a good deal is a bonus.
